incumbent.name: Terry R. Modesitt
incumbent.summary: Terry R. Modesitt has been Vigo County prosecutor since January 1, 2007 {vigo_ipac} and is running for re-election {in_list}. In 2022 he defeated Democrat Johnny Edward Vaughn, his opponent again this year, with about 61% of the unofficial vote {vigo_2022_results}.
record: Before taking office: served as a deputy prosecutor {vigo_ipac}; in 2022 he said that when first elected he "was 49 and had been a trial deputy here at the Prosecutor's Office for 22 years" {vigo_wtwo_2022}.
January 1, 2007: Took office as Vigo County prosecutor {vigo_ipac}.
November 2022: Re-elected over Vaughn, 16,320 votes (60.89%) to 10,481 (39.11%), with 88 of 89 precincts reporting (final unofficial results) {vigo_2022_results}.

2022: Said the job involved managing 50 employees and budgets for several departments, including Adult Protective Services and Victims' Assistance, and that the office's case backlog had grown to about 4,500 during the COVID-19 pandemic {vigo_wtwo_2022}.
No 2025–2026 reporting on the office's caseloads, staffing or budget could be fetched for this profile.

race_context: Rematch of 2022: incumbent Republican Terry Modesitt, prosecutor since 2007, again faces Democrat Johnny Vaughn, whom he defeated 60.89% to 39.11% in the 2022 general election (unofficial) {vigo_ipac}{vigo_2022_results}.
Modesitt filed on January 16, 2026 and Vaughn on January 30, 2026 {in_list}{vigo_trib_filing}. No May 5, 2026 primary results for this office were found.

Key differences in 2022: Vaughn proposed attending every initial hearing to review bond and said he would not prosecute small cannabis-use charges; Modesitt emphasized experience and managing the case backlog and jail population {vigo_wtwo_2022}. No 2026 statements by either candidate were found.
No 2026 forums or debates featuring this race were found.

candidates.summary: Vaughn is a Terre Haute criminal-law attorney who was the Democratic nominee against Modesitt in 2022 and filed again in January 2026 {vigo_wtwo_2022}{vigo_trib_filing}.
background: Attended McLean Alternative High School in Terre Haute, Ivy Tech Community College and Indiana State University, and law school at IU's Indianapolis campus {vigo_wtwo_2022}.
Practiced criminal law; in November 2022 he said, "I've been a criminal attorney for over a year now" {vigo_wtwo_2022}.
Ran for prosecutor in 2022 as Johnny Edward Vaughn and received 10,481 votes (39.11%, unofficial) {vigo_2022_results}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Democrat for Vigo County prosecutor on January 30, 2026 {vigo_trib_filing}{in_list}; listed as the Democratic nominee {in_list}. Primary results were not found.

items: In 2022 he said he would not prosecute small cannabis-use charges, in order to focus on violent crimes {vigo_wtwo_2022}. It was not found whether he holds the same position in 2026.
In 2022 he said he would attend every initial hearing for defendants to check that bond is fair {vigo_wtwo_2022}.

on_incumbent: No 2026 statements by Vaughn about Modesitt's record were found. In 2022 he said his priority would be presence in the office and in public: "I will be in the courtrooms" {vigo_wtwo_2022}.
plans: 2022 plans: be present in courtrooms and the office, attend initial hearings to review bond, and redirect resources from small cannabis cases to violent crime {vigo_wtwo_2022}. No 2026 platform was found.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: All position statements found date from the 2022 campaign; no 2026 interview, website or questionnaire was found.

Search-result snippets (2022 coverage) said he proposed removing low-level marijuana cases in Terre Haute City Court and speeding trials by sending plea offers and discovery sooner, and that he worked as a public defender in CHINS cases; the full article could not be fetched, so these are unverified.
A lawyer directory in search results lists a Johnny Edward Vaughn with Vaughn Law LLC in Terre Haute; not confirmed on a fetched page.

candidates.summary: Modesitt has been Vigo County prosecutor since January 1, 2007, after serving as a deputy prosecutor {vigo_ipac}.
background: Undergraduate degree from Indiana State University; J.D. from Indiana University in Indianapolis {vigo_ipac}.
Trial deputy in the Vigo County Prosecutor's Office for 22 years before becoming prosecutor, by his own account in 2022 {vigo_wtwo_2022}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Republican on January 16, 2026, and is listed as the Republican nominee {in_list}. Primary results were not found.

items: In 2022 he said he aimed to keep managing a case backlog that grew to about 4,500 during COVID-19 and to keep prosecutions efficient to prevent jail overcrowding: "Let's try to be as efficient as possible moving forward even once we get in the new jail" {vigo_wtwo_2022}.
In 2022 he said, "I support all the drug recovery programs here locally, those type of things too" {vigo_wtwo_2022}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. In 2022 he said lengthy legal experience is key to being prepared for the job {vigo_wtwo_2022}. No 2026 statements about Vaughn were found.
plans: 2022 plans: continue managing the backlog and keep prosecutions efficient to limit jail overcrowding {vigo_wtwo_2022}. No 2026 platform was found.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: All position statements found date from the 2022 campaign; no 2026 interview, website or questionnaire was found.

Search-result snippets from undated WTHI stories said Modesitt described his office as about ten deputy prosecutors short of an ideal 29 and said salary increases helped recruiting; those pages returned 404 and the claims are unverified.
Search-result snippets from 2022 coverage quoted him opposing prosecutors choosing which laws to enforce and citing more than 100,000 cases prosecuted; not verified on a fetched page.
